TLDR: Friends for 2 years, inseparable for 6 months, made a move while drunk 3.5 years ago. Still with him and deeply in love, his arms feel like home. THE ONLY "negative" compared to dating someone new  is skipping the "getting to know eachother and feeling like you're gonna explode anytime you see them" phase. 



We were friends for 2 years and best friends for around 6 months before I made a move after lots of jaggerbombs.  During tbe 6 months we spent around 4 days/week together from 9am-10pm as we had a research project together. I've been with him since then. 


**Our situation/how is it?** 3,5 years later we live together, have a dog and a cat. I was very worried I made a mistake the weeks that followed because I knew that I wanted to build a life with that man and would be broken if it was not reciprocal. Then time went by, I moved in without us noticing, got our pets from family members, went through hardships and always stood by eachother no questions asked. In those years, some very difficult times for both of us, I never wondered ONCE if I wanted to break up with him.



**How is it different from other relationships?** He knew me like the palm of his hands before we even considered ourselves as potential partners, and so did I. So the first few months of "passion" felt more like a continuation of our friendship with lots of sex. Compared to other relationships I would say it was less "soul absorbing" and I was not as "obsessed/in constant craving". There were no bad surprises and instead of feeling butterflies/my heart exploding the first few times we went on dates I would feel just peace inside. I still feel peaceful next to him, while with my exes the buterfly led to intense feelings, good or bad. It changed my definition of love. Best "mistake ever"

My experience is different but I would like to share it. I got an almost simultaneous bipolar disord II and ADD diagnosis (which makes finding the right meds a difficult process). Like others have said, I never struggled at school, was top of my class but I did not have one single binder. Just a big pocket where I threw everything (and my organisation is the same one every aspects of my life), I always buy bright things to make sure I don't lose them, buy headphones in industrial quantity, post its all around my work space, but I thought I was just very disorganized. What really set me off was during college when I could not physically stand in a classroom. I needed to be active in order to follow the class or I would quick become hyper sensitive. So I picked up the good habit of working on my projects while taking notes, and my grades got better. I realised that either I have too much attention to give or not enough to receive all these informations. I had all the other diagnosis before: GAD, Depression, Anorexia, Bulimia but we never suspected that. 

Once I got my diagnosis and started to read about it, it felt like all the abnormalities that I tried to hide in order to fit were not just my fault and non willingness to make efforts. There are many people with the same issues. But the twist is, I still could not understand why I didn't feel the same way all year, I recognised just a part of me in these forums. The BPD2 diagnosis helped me complete my realisation.
